# Polkadot host capabilities

> What a Product (a web app running inside the Polkadot app) can and cannot do. Each answer is
> measured from inside the app on a real phone, with working code for each capability. Results are
> keyed by date, TrUAPI wire codec, product-sdk-host version and OS, because no host API reports
> the app's version. Everything here is dated: re-check against the newest run before relying on a
> "not available".

Read this first:

- Build your SDK against the wire codec the app speaks. As of 2026-09-19 the Android app answers
  codec 1 only: pin @parity/product-sdk-host 0.19.1 and @parity/truapi 0.13.1 exactly. On a mismatch
  every host call hangs.
- Give every host call a deadline. Many never settle when they can't do what was asked.
- Location is not available to a Product (the host grants it, and the WebView still refuses).
  Design flows that need no GPS.
- Store on Bulletin with getPreimageManager().submit(), not cloudStorage.upload (Invalid: Payment).
  Data is public by BLAKE2b-256 hash and lasts about two weeks.
- The Statement Store holds 512 bytes per statement and about 1 KiB per account. Use it to
  rendezvous; it reaches other phones.
- Nothing leaves the app as a file. Export by copying text.
- IndexedDB, CacheStorage, service workers, web push and Notification are absent. Use host local
  storage and host notifications.
- Publish with a local deploy key, not the phone's signer.

## Capabilities

- [Location](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Baronvonbonbon/polkadot-host-capabilities/main/capabilities/location.md): not available; how to detect it, and a design that settles without GPS
- [Bulletin storage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Baronvonbonbon/polkadot-host-capabilities/main/capabilities/bulletin-storage.md): uploads through the host, costs, sizes, retention, lookups
- [Statement Store](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Baronvonbonbon/polkadot-host-capabilities/main/capabilities/statement-store.md): signed 512-byte messages between phones; limits and code
- [Permissions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Baronvonbonbon/polkadot-host-capabilities/main/capabilities/permissions.md): host permissions and web permissions, and why a host grant doesn't open the web API
- [Identity and accounts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Baronvonbonbon/polkadot-host-capabilities/main/capabilities/identity-and-accounts.md): product accounts, deterministic entropy, signing, EIP-712
- [Chain access](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Baronvonbonbon/polkadot-host-capabilities/main/capabilities/chain-access.md): devnet chains and their genesis hashes, chain specs, the host RPC provider
- [Notifications](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Baronvonbonbon/polkadot-host-capabilities/main/capabilities/notifications.md): host notifications, including scheduled ones with the app closed
- [Storage on the device](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Baronvonbonbon/polkadot-host-capabilities/main/capabilities/local-storage.md): host local storage, and which web storage exists
- [Gas and signing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Baronvonbonbon/polkadot-host-capabilities/main/capabilities/gas-and-signing.md): PGAS, the testnet gas asset; the host's contract-gas allowance; whether signing needs a tap
- [Payments](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Baronvonbonbon/polkadot-host-capabilities/main/capabilities/payments.md): the payment manager's balance never arrives yet
- [App and system](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Baronvonbonbon/polkadot-host-capabilities/main/capabilities/app-and-system.md): detection, handshake, app version, navigateTo, theme, chat, new builds
- [Files and sharing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Baronvonbonbon/polkadot-host-capabilities/main/capabilities/files-and-sharing.md): picking works, downloads and share don't, clipboard write only
- [Media and calls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Baronvonbonbon/polkadot-host-capabilities/main/capabilities/media-and-calls.md): camera, microphone, QR codes, WebRTC status
- [Compute and crypto](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Baronvonbonbon/polkadot-host-capabilities/main/capabilities/compute-and-crypto.md): WASM, WebCrypto, workers, no SharedArrayBuffer; timings on a phone
- [Network](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Baronvonbonbon/polkadot-host-capabilities/main/capabilities/network.md): fetch, WebSocket, sendBeacon refused, the devnet IPFS gateway
- [Sensors and hardware](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Baronvonbonbon/polkadot-host-capabilities/main/capabilities/sensors-and-hardware.md): motion sensors work; Bluetooth, USB, NFC don't
- [UI and display](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Baronvonbonbon/polkadot-host-capabilities/main/capabilities/ui-and-display.md): no fullscreen, no AVIF, wake lock works

## Pitfalls

- [Wire codec](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Baronvonbonbon/polkadot-host-capabilities/main/pitfalls/wire-codec.md): the exact SDK pins that work with the current app
- [Host calls can hang](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Baronvonbonbon/polkadot-host-capabilities/main/pitfalls/host-calls-can-hang.md): which calls go silent, and the deadlines to use
- [SDK gotchas](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Baronvonbonbon/polkadot-host-capabilities/main/pitfalls/sdk-gotchas.md): two Result conventions, the BulletinAllowance spelling, createApp's environment
- [Deploy with a key](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Baronvonbonbon/polkadot-host-capabilities/main/pitfalls/deploy-with-a-key.md): why phone-signed .dot names get stranded, and the fix
- [DotNS registrar moved](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Baronvonbonbon/polkadot-host-capabilities/main/pitfalls/dotns-registrar-moved.md): current devnet DotNS contract addresses

## Data

- [Matrix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Baronvonbonbon/polkadot-host-capabilities/main/matrix.md): every probe in every run

- [FARE](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Baronvonbonbon/polkadot-host-capabilities/main/sources/fare.md): GPS-free settlement, Statement Store signalling, Bulletin as evidence

<<< capabilities/app-and-system.md >>>

---
capability: The host container, the app, navigation and theme
probes: [host.system.container, host.system.handshake, host.system.version, host.system.createApp, host.system.navigateTo, host.theme.subscribe, host.chat.list, host.limits.bridgePayload, host.limits.concurrency, web.limits.backgrounding]
---

# The host container, the app, navigation and theme

**Status (2026-09-19, codec 1, Android):** detection, the handshake, `createApp`, theme and chat
work, and so does `navigateTo` to an outside URL. No host API tells you the app's version.

## Detect the host, then handshake

```ts
import { isInsideContainer } from "@parity/product-sdk-host";
// Outside the app nobody answers this message round-trip, so it needs a deadline.
const inHost = await Promise.race([isInsideContainer(), new Promise<boolean>((r) => setTimeout(() => r(false), 1500))]);
```

The handshake is where a **wire codec mismatch** shows up: every host call after it hangs. Pin the
SDK to the codec the app speaks ([pitfalls/wire-codec.md](../pitfalls/wire-codec.md)).

## Which app build am I on?

**You can't tell.** No truapi namespace has a version call (`system` offers `handshake`,
`featureSupported` and `navigateTo`). The user agent's Chromium version is the Android **system
WebView**, updated through the Play Store separately from the Polkadot app, so it doesn't identify
the app either. This repository keys runs by date, wire codec, SDK and OS instead. If you can read
the version off the phone (Settings → About), put it in `runtime.appVersion`.

## How big one host call can be

A 4 MiB value crosses the bridge both ways (host local storage, 2026-09-19 12:55), and 16 MiB is
refused with an error. Writing 8 MiB killed the page. Treat **4 MiB as the ceiling for any single
host call.**

## Calling the host a lot

200 host calls fired at once all answered correctly, in 1.7 s (10 took 175 ms, 50 took 828 ms).
There's no need to serialise calls by hand. (2026-09-19)

## Getting a new build onto the phone

Close the product, then **close the Polkadot app itself**, then open the product again. Closing only
the product kept showing the previous build (almanac). Show a build id in your footer so you can
tell which build is running.

## navigateTo

`navigateTo(url)` asks the host to open a URL, gated by the `OpenUrl` device permission. **Don't
pass your own page's URL.** An honoured navigation to it reloads the product, which the 09:25 run on
2026-09-19 mistook for a bug until the probe was read. At 10:05, given an outside URL (a GitHub
page), the host **accepted the call in 28 ms, and the product kept running.** Whether the URL opened
in the system browser wasn't recorded.

## Theme

`getThemeProvider().subscribeTheme(cb)` delivers the current theme at once and then any changes.
**It follows the host's theme, not the phone's.** almanac saw the host dark (`berlinNight`) while the
phone was set to light (almanac P12). Style against the host theme.

## Chat

`getChatManager().subscribeChatList(cb)` is reachable, and 0 rooms were visible to a new product.
`registerRoom` and `registerBot` create lasting state on the host side and have not been probed.

## Measured

<<< capabilities/bulletin-storage.md >>>

---
capability: Bulletin storage (uploads and reads through the host)
probes: [host.cloud.allowance, host.preimage.submit, host.cloud.upload, host.cloud.roundTrip, host.cloud.read, host.preimage.lookup, host.cloud.seal, host.limits.retention, host.limits.preimageSize, host.limits.bulletinQuota]
---

# Bulletin storage

**Status (2026-09-19, codec 1, Android): works through the host's preimage manager. It does not work
through the SDK's `cloudStorage.upload`.** Data is public by content hash and lasts about two
weeks.

## Use it

1. Request a `BulletinAllowance`. Spell it exactly that way, even though the type says otherwise.
2. Request the `PreimageSubmit` permission.
3. Upload with `getPreimageManager().submit(bytes)`. It returns a BLAKE2b-256 key.
4. Read with `lookup(key, callback)`.

```ts
import { formatHostError, getPreimageManager, requestPermission, requestResourceAllocation } from "@parity/product-sdk-host";

// The TypeScript type spells it "BulletInAllowance", and that spelling throws. Only this one allocates.
await requestResourceAllocation([{ tag: "BulletinAllowance", value: undefined } as never]);
const p = await requestPermission({ tag: "PreimageSubmit", value: undefined });
if (!p.ok || !p.value) throw new Error(p.ok ? "user said no" : formatHostError(p.error));
const manager = await getPreimageManager();            // null when the host offers no storage
const key = await manager!.submit(bytes);              // hex BLAKE2b-256; give it a deadline (1 MiB took 41 s)

// A lookup is a subscription that stays SILENT until the bytes arrive. There is no "not found".
function get(key: `0x${string}`, ms = 30_000): Promise<Uint8Array | null> {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const sub = manager!.lookup(key, (b) => { if (b) { clearTimeout(t); sub.unsubscribe(); resolve(b); } });
    const t = setTimeout(() => { sub.unsubscribe(); resolve(null); }, ms);
  });
}
```

## Who pays, and how much fits

- **The payer is a slot account the host keeps the key for.** No Product API names it. The
  allowance reaches it by XCM from the People chain. Each claim is **10 transactions and 4 MiB**,
  and it expires about 14 days (201,600 blocks) after it lands. The account holds no balance, so
  this is quota, never a fee. (almanac P6b)
- **One upload is one transaction, charged at exactly its own size.** 16 KiB took 6.7 s, 64 KiB
  10.0 s, 256 KiB 16.8 s and **1 MiB 41.4 s** on a Pixel 10 Pro XL. Each came back byte for byte.
  (almanac P6c)
- **Allowances and slot accounts are per product id**, meaning the `.dot` label. Two names give two
  separate quotas.

## Don't

- **Don't use `app.cloudStorage.upload`.** It signs with product account #0, which holds no Bulletin
  authorization, so every upload is refused with `Invalid: Payment`, even right after `Allocated`.
  (almanac P6, read on chain with a positive control.) sonde saw the same on 2026-09-19 at 10:53:
  a 26-byte canary failed with `ProductCloudStorageError` in 3.7 s, straight after `Allocated`.
- **Don't expect SHA-256 CIDs to come back through the host.** The host's lookup takes a bare
  32-byte digest and finds BLAKE2b-256 content only. A `bafkrei…` or `bafybei…` CID, like the ones
  `pad` makes for a site bundle, waits out the SDK's 30 s timeout instead of failing. The devnet
  IPFS gateway serves both kinds. (almanac P7)
- **Don't treat a lookup that never calls back as proof of anything.** The read-only lookup probe
  (almanac's fixture key) got no callback in 5 s at 10:38, 10:53 and 11:31, then answered at
  14:06, on the same phone. Give lookups a generous timeout and retry.
- **Don't treat silence as "not found".** A lookup of absent content never calls back. Always race
  it against a timer.
- **Don't store anything readable.** Anyone can fetch it by hash. Encrypt first; WebCrypto
  AES-GCM works (`host.cloud.seal`). Treat ciphertext as possibly permanent and plaintext
  retention as possibly shorter than you hoped.

## Measured by sonde

`getPreimageManager().submit()` stored 64 random bytes in **29.8 s** and read them back by key in
154 ms, byte for byte (2026-09-19 12:55). almanac's 256-byte upload took 4.1–8.8 s, so upload time
varies a lot. Show progress, and give uploads a generous deadline.

## Reading through the SDK works for BLAKE2b content

On 2026-09-19 at 10:05, `app.cloudStorage.fetch()` of a 79-byte BLAKE2b-256 blob, stored five days
earlier, came back in **245 ms**, and its CID verified. The same call on a SHA-256 CID times out
after 30 s.

## Retention

Measured about two weeks, while the docs say content persists. almanac follows two fixture CIDs
from a desktop (`npm run retention` in almanac). The first 15-day checks fall on 2026-09-28 and
2026-09-29. In the app, sonde's `host.limits.retention` looks up its own earlier uploads at the
start of each run: at 14:06 it found 2 of 2, the oldest 0.03 days old. That only shows the lookup
path works, not how long content lasts; the ages grow as runs continue. Plan for expiry: FARE uses the ~14-day life as a dispute-evidence window
([sources/fare.md](../sources/fare.md)).

## Measured

Latest detail per probe:

- `host.cloud.allowance` — Never settled after 150s. A call that neither resolves nor rejects is worse than one that fails.
- `host.preimage.submit` — **Retracted, a probe bug:** Not measured: sonde's spend gate needs an identified chain, and getChainSpec answered for no chain this run. Fixed in sonde (89bab46): it falls back to isChainSupported. The run said: No genesis hash resolved yet — run host.chain.genesis first. Spending on an unidentified chain is refused.
- `host.cloud.upload` — **Retracted, a probe bug:** Not measured: sonde's spend gate needs an identified chain, and getChainSpec answered for no chain this run. Fixed in sonde (89bab46): it falls back to isChainSupported. The run said: No genesis hash resolved yet — run host.chain.genesis first. Spending on an unidentified chain is refused.
- `host.cloud.roundTrip` — Needs "host.cloud.upload", which came back skip. Running anyway would test a placeholder.
- `host.cloud.read` — Fetched 0.1 KiB in 52 ms and the CID verifies. Reads work.
- `host.preimage.lookup` — Lookup answered.
- `host.cloud.seal` — Sealed a placeholder in 3 ms (run the camera probe first for a real payload).
- `host.limits.retention` — 2 of 2 earlier uploads still readable; oldest found 0.0 days. — measures: `tracked=2` `found=2` `oldestFoundDays=0.03` `youngestMissingDays=-1`
- `host.limits.preimageSize` — Opt-in (spends-quota) — not selected for this run. Run it from its card, or tick the opt-in box.
- `host.limits.bulletinQuota` — Opt-in (spends-quota) — not selected for this run. Run it from its card, or tick the opt-in box.

<<< capabilities/chain-access.md >>>

---
capability: Chain access (chain specs, JSON-RPC, direct WebSocket)
probes: [host.system.featureSupported, host.chain.genesis, host.chain.provider, web.net.websocket]
---

# Chain access

**Status (2026-09-19, codec 1, Android): the host returns a chain spec for Paseo Asset Hub and
builds a JSON-RPC provider for it.** For the devnet's own "Next" chains, `getChainSpec` apparently
gave no answer (inferred from timing, see below). A direct WebSocket from the WebView works.

**Confirmed at 10:53:** with each chain named in the result, `getChainSpec` answered for **Paseo
Asset Hub only**. It gave no answer for Paseo Bulletin Next, Paseo People Next, Paseo Asset Hub
Next, or Polkadot Asset Hub.

**What the 10:05 run showed.** sonde asked for five chains in order, giving each 6 s: Bulletin Next,
People Next, Asset Hub Next, Paseo Asset Hub, then Polkadot Asset Hub. The probe took 24.3 s and
resolved **Paseo Asset Hub** (`0xd6eec261…`). That fit three silent 6 s waits for the Next chains,
then a slow answer for Paseo Asset Hub. The 10:53 run confirmed it. Then
`getHostProvider` for Paseo Asset Hub was built in 34 ms. The devnet host still uses the Next chains
for storage (`createApp` on `devnet` works, and so do uploads through the host). They just don't come
back from `getChainSpec`.

**It is also flaky for Paseo Asset Hub.** It answered in 4 of the 5 runs on 2026-09-19. At 14:06
**no chain answered** in 32.9 s, and every probe that spends refused to run because it had no chain
to check against its allowlist. `isChainSupported` answers in about 30 ms on every run. So don't make
`getChainSpec` a hard prerequisite: race it, and if nothing comes back, fall back to
`isChainSupported` over the genesis hashes you already know. sonde does this from build 14:10:55Z.

## The chains a devnet host carries

The Products devnet runs "Next" chains. A host build carries a fixed set of them. Each genesis
below was read off its own RPC with `chain_getBlockHash(0)` on 2026-09-19:

| Chain | Genesis | RPC |
|---|---|---|
| Paseo Asset Hub Next | `0x4349b00e54897e21196fd331015fc5be0f14e118beb0375ed2bb1793737bb57a` | `wss://paseo-asset-hub-next-rpc.polkadot.io` |
| Paseo People Next | `0x4a2b5b737de1da59e209b0000a876ec2fa20035dc34fd292a848da32d255ad48` | `wss://paseo-people-next-system-rpc.polkadot.io` |
| Paseo Bulletin Next | `0x8cfe6717dc4becfda2e13c488a1e2061ff2dfee96e7d031157f72d36716c0a22` | `wss://paseo-bulletin-next-rpc.polkadot.io` |
| Paseo Asset Hub (public testnet) | `0xd6eec26135305a8ad257a20d003357284c8aa03d0bdb2b357ab0a22371e11ef2` | `wss://asset-hub-paseo-rpc.n.dwellir.com` |

DotNS and FARE's contracts live on Paseo Asset Hub's EVM, `https://eth-rpc-testnet.polkadot.io/`,
chain id 420420417.

**`createApp`'s cloud storage environment must match the one you published under.** The SDK
defaults to `"paseo"`. A devnet host doesn't carry that Bulletin chain, so `createApp` throws
`Chain 0x8cfe6717… is not supported by the current host`, and everything that depends on storage
fails after it.

## Use it

```ts
import { getChainSpec, getHostProvider, isChainSupported } from "@parity/product-sdk-host";
const supported = await isChainSupported(genesis);   // Result<boolean>
const spec = await getChainSpec(genesis);            // Result<spec | null>; race it (see below)
const provider = await getHostProvider(genesis);     // a JSON-RPC provider routed by the host
```

- **Race every chain call against a deadline.** Asked about a genesis it doesn't carry, the host
  may never answer. It should say "not supported", and in the 2026-09-19 run it said nothing for
  45 s. See [pitfalls/host-calls-can-hang.md](../pitfalls/host-calls-can-hang.md).
- A direct `WebSocket` to a public RPC also works from inside the app. It connected to
  `wss://rpc.polkadot.io`, and almanac P10 reached People-chain nodes offering `statement_*` and
  Bulletin nodes. No content policy blocked it.

---
capability: Compute, crypto and workers
probes: [web.compute.wasm, web.compute.wasmFeatures, web.compute.subtleCrypto, web.compute.structuredClone, web.compute.worker, web.compute.sharedWorker, web.compute.sharedArrayBuffer, web.platform.timerResolution, web.platform.memory, web.platform.scheduler, web.platform.locks, web.limits.groth16, web.limits.wasmMemory, web.limits.memoryCeiling]
---

# Compute, crypto and workers

**Status (2026-09-19, codec 1, Android): fast and complete for a single thread.** There is no
`SharedArrayBuffer`, because the page is not cross-origin isolated, so there are no WASM threads.

- **WebAssembly** compiles and runs, with SIMD available, so crypto libraries take their fast path.
- **`crypto.subtle`** supports every algorithm tested, **including Ed25519 and X25519**.
- **Dedicated Workers** work, including one started from a blob URL. SharedWorker is absent.
- **`SharedArrayBuffer` is not defined** (`crossOriginIsolated` is false). Multi-threaded WASM
  builds (some zk provers, some argon2/scrypt builds) must fall back to single-threaded.
- **Timer resolution:** `performance.now()` ticks at 0.1 ms.

## Real numbers on a phone (Pixel 10 Pro XL, almanac P11)

| Work | Time |
|---|---|
| scrypt r=8, N=2¹⁵ | 101 ms |
| scrypt r=8, N=2¹⁶ | 169 ms |
| scrypt r=8, N=2¹⁷ | 328 ms |
| XChaCha20-Poly1305, 1 MiB | 24 ms encrypt, 8 ms decrypt |
| BLAKE2b-256, 1 MiB | 18 ms |
| AES-256-GCM, 3.2 KiB (FARE) | 1 ms |
| secp256k1 EIP-712 sign + recover (FARE, sonde) | 2–3 ms |

This is a flagship phone; expect roughly 2–3× slower on mid-range hardware. FARE also runs a real
Groth16 proof for delivery proximity. Its proving time on a phone isn't in this repository yet.

capability: Files, sharing and the clipboard

# Files, sharing and the clipboard

**Status (2026-09-19, codec 1, Android): files come in; nothing leaves as a file.** Reading a
picked file works. Downloads, file sharing, Web Share and print do nothing. Writing to the
clipboard works; reading from it is blocked.

| Path | Result |
|---|---|
| `<input type="file">` | works: a 4.5 MB PDF and a 1.5 MB PNG were read (almanac P4) |
| `showOpenFilePicker()` | works |
| `showSaveFilePicker()` / `showDirectoryPicker()` | rejected in 11 ms with "The user aborted a request". That is too fast for a person, so most likely no picker was shown. **Treat as unavailable** |
| `<a download>`, blob or data links | **do nothing** (almanac P4) |
| `navigator.share` (text, URL, files) | **absent** |
| `window.print()` | does nothing (almanac P4) |
| `navigator.clipboard.writeText` | works; **5 MB accepted** in one call (2026-09-19). Whether a paste elsewhere receives all of it was not checked |
| `navigator.clipboard.readText` | **blocked**: "Read permission denied", even after the host granted `Clipboard` |

## What to do

- **Export by copying text.** almanac copies backups and the visit summary as text, and shows the
  text on screen in case the clipboard refuses.
- **Import by picking a file, or by pasting into a text field.** Pasting through the keyboard's own
  UI works where `readText()` doesn't.
- **Exchange between two phones with QR codes.** `BarcodeDetector` is built in on Android, and the
  camera works ([media-and-calls.md](media-and-calls.md)).

<<< capabilities/gas-and-signing.md >>>

---
capability: Gas and signing
probes: [host.gas.smartContractAllowance, host.gas.autoSigning]
---

# Gas and signing

**Status (2026-09-19): not yet measured on a device.** truapi declares a host-granted gas allowance
for contract calls and a tap-free signing mode. sonde asks for both from build 15:15:07Z. What
follows was read off the chains and the SDK's types on 2026-09-19.

## PGAS, the testnet gas asset

- **PGAS is asset `2000000000` in the `Assets` pallet** on Paseo Asset Hub and Paseo Asset Hub
  Next. Polkadot and Kusama Asset Hub have no PGAS pallet, so it is a testnet-only rail.
- **It is minted by `Pgas.claim_pgas(slot_index, target)`, an unsigned call.** The `AsPgas`
  transaction extension checks a ring-VRF personhood proof over the call, so the chain learns
  "some person claimed", not which one, and `target` can be any account.
- **Fees can be paid in it.** The `PgasAllowance` pallet emits `PGASFeePaid { who, actual_fee }`
  when a transaction's fee is taken in PGAS and burned.
- The asset has no metadata (no symbol, no decimals). One holder read on 2026-09-19 held
  10,000,000 raw units.

```ts
// Storage key for an account's PGAS: Assets.Account(2000000000, accountId)
const PREFIX =
  "0x682a59d51ab9e48a8c8cc418ff9708d2b99d880ec681799c0cf30e8886371da946de6e688c2258c9eb90a9b5c834b13d00943577";
const key = PREFIX + hex(blake2b(accountId, { dkLen: 16 })) + hex(accountId);
// state_getStorage(key) → AssetAccount; the balance is the first 16 bytes, little-endian.
```

## The host's allowance

`requestResourceAllocation([{ tag: "SmartContractAllowance", value: index }])` is described in
truapi as a "pre-warmed PGAS balance for the product account at this derivation index". The host
may also grant it implicitly on the first transaction. Only the host can make the ring-VRF proof,
so a Product can't claim PGAS for itself; it gets PGAS through this call, to a product account
the host picks by index.

- **Don't use it to fund a private account.** Product accounts derive from the user's root public
  key, so anyone who knows that key can link them.

## AutoSigning

`AutoSigning` is also a `requestResourceAllocation` tag. `product-sdk-terminal`'s types say it is
`NotAvailable` on the Android and iOS wallets, which would make every host-signed transaction a
tap. `host.gas.autoSigning` asks for it and times a signature to find out.

## Measured

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `host.gas.smartContractAllowance`  | — | — | — | — |
| `host.gas.autoSigning`  | — | — | — | — |

---
capability: Identity, accounts and signing
probes: [host.account.connect, host.account.userId, host.account.productAccounts, host.account.legacyAccounts, host.account.deriveEntropy, host.account.signMessage, host.account.eip712, host.account.anonymousAlias, web.identity.webauthnSupport, web.identity.webauthnCreate, web.identity.credentialManagement, web.identity.fedcm, web.identity.digitalCredentials]
---

# Identity, accounts and signing

**Status (2026-09-19, codec 1, Android):** connect, product accounts, deterministic entropy and
host signing all work. The Ring VRF anonymous alias returns `null`. WebAuthn is absent.

## Accounts a Product sees

- **Product accounts** derive from the user's root *public* key, the product id and an index:
  `deriveProductAccountPublicKey(parentPublicKey, productId, index)` in `product-sdk-keys`. Indices
  give distinct keys (0, 1, 2 and 7 were checked). The catch: **anyone who knows a user's root
  account can compute all their product accounts.** Per-index accounts do not hide a user from
  someone who knows the root.
- **The app often shows a Product only product account #0**, so there is no root to derive from
  inside the app (almanac P8).
- **Different jobs are signed by different accounts.** Uploads through `cloudStorage` are signed by
  product account #0. Statements are signed by the allowance account, which is none of #0–#2.
  Bulletin preimages are paid by a hidden slot account (almanac P6b, P8).
- `getUserId()` returns a stable per-user handle. `getLegacyAccounts()` returned 0 accounts.

```ts
import { createApp } from "@parity/product-sdk";
const app = await createApp({ name: PRODUCT_ID, cloudStorage: { environment: "devnet" } });
const r = await app.wallet.connect();
app.wallet.selectAccount(r.accounts[0].address);   // connected but unselected: storage calls stall, not error
```

## Keys a Product can keep for itself

`deriveEntropy(input)` is **deterministic per product**. It gives the same bytes for the same input,
across app restarts and across new builds of the product (almanac P2). Seed an app-local key with it
and the key regenerates from nothing. Reinstall and a second phone are not measured yet.

**EVM signatures:** the host signs sr25519. A contract's `ecrecover` needs secp256k1. An app-local
secp256k1 key signs EIP-712 in 2–3 ms, and `verifyTypedData` recovers it exactly (FARE and sonde).
So attestations a contract checks are signed locally, and the host signs chain transactions.

## Signing through the host

`app.wallet.signMessage` shows the host's prompt and returns 64 bytes. AutoSigning reports
`NotAvailable`, so every signature is a tap. The promise settles only when the user answers.

## Publishing is a different story

`pad`, the deploy tool, signs through the phone as a hidden product account. The app never reveals
that account, and it changed between app releases. So a `.dot` name registered from the phone can
end up owned by an account the phone no longer signs as. Publish with a local deploy key:
[pitfalls/deploy-with-a-key.md](../pitfalls/deploy-with-a-key.md).

<<< capabilities/local-storage.md >>>

---
capability: Storage on the device
probes: [host.localStorage.roundTrip, web.storage.webStorage, web.storage.indexedDb, web.storage.cacheStorage, web.storage.quota, web.storage.cookies, web.storage.storageAccessApi, web.filesystem.opfs, host.limits.localStorageCeiling]
---

# Storage on the device

**Status (2026-09-19, codec 1, Android): use host local storage.** Web `localStorage` and OPFS also
work. IndexedDB and CacheStorage are absent, and cookies don't persist.

## Host local storage

The host keeps a store per product id. It holds strings, JSON and bytes.

```ts
import { getHostLocalStorage } from "@parity/product-sdk-host";
const store = await getHostLocalStorage();   // null outside the app
await store!.writeBytes("k", bytes);  await store!.readBytes("k");
await store!.writeJSON("j", obj);     await store!.readJSON("j");
await store!.writeString("s", "v");   await store!.readString("s");
await store!.clear("k");
```

- **Size:** one 4 MiB record was written and read back in 1.2–1.3 s (almanac P1), and again by
  sonde (2026-09-19 12:55). A 16 MiB write is refused cleanly. **Writing an 8 MiB record killed
  the page**: the product was reloaded mid-run. **Keep single records at 4 MiB or under.**
- **Survives:** an app restart, and publishing a new build of the product (almanac P1). An update
  of the Polkadot app and a reinstall are **not measured yet**. Neither is whether the store is in
  phone backups (almanac P5).
- **Namespaced by product id.** Change the `.dot` label and the data is gone from the new name's
  point of view.
- An empty read may come back as a zero-length value. almanac treats empty as absent.

## Web storage inside the app

| API | Result |
|---|---|
| `localStorage` / `sessionStorage` | works |
| Origin Private File System | works (64 KiB written and read back) |
| IndexedDB | **absent**: `indexedDB` is undefined |
| CacheStorage | **absent** |
| Cookies | `document.cookie` writes don't persist, even though the document is top-level |
| `navigator.storage.persist()` | best-effort only (evictable) |

Libraries that assume IndexedDB (idb-keyval, Dexie, localForage's default driver, most wallet
SDKs' session stores) fail inside the app. Give them a host-storage adapter.

- `web.storage.quota` — Quota reported; storage is best-effort (evictable).
- `web.storage.cookies` — A first-party cookie did not persist. In a framed context this is partitioning or third-party cookie blocking, not a broken engine.

  ```
  navigator.cookieEnabled: true
  document.cookie write : did not persist
  cookieStore API       : present
  cookieStore.getAll    : 0 cookie(s)
  hasStorageAccess      : true
  framed                : false
  ```
- `web.storage.storageAccessApi` — Present.
- `web.filesystem.opfs` — Wrote and read back 64.0 KiB byte-for-byte.
- `host.limits.localStorageCeiling` — Opt-in (crash-risk) — not selected for this run. Run it from its card, or tick the opt-in box.

<<< capabilities/location.md >>>

---
capability: Location
probes: [host.permissions.location, web.sensors.geolocation, web.sensors.geolocationWatch]
---

# Location

**Status (2026-09-19, codec 1, Android 16): not available to a Product.** The host grants its
`Location` permission, and `navigator.geolocation` still fails straight away. Design for no GPS.

## What happens

An Android WebView only gets location if the host app holds the OS permission **and** answers the
WebView's `onGeolocationPermissionsShowPrompt` callback. The Polkadot app does neither for a Product:

```
navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition → error code 1, "User denied Geolocation"
permissions.query({name:"geolocation"})  → "prompt"   (before and after)
```

`prompt` means the permission was never decided: no dialog was shown and nothing was stored. A real
refusal by the user leaves `denied`. So the pattern **denied with the state still `prompt`** means the
host never answered the callback. sonde calls this `host-callback-missing`.

truapi declares `requestDevicePermission("Location")`, and the host grants it. Even with Android's
own location permission allowed for the app as well (2026-09-19 10:38), nothing changes. Measured 2026-09-19,
granting it changes nothing: web geolocation run straight after still fails the same way. The two
permission systems are not connected. Upstream:
[products-devnet-issues#7](https://github.com/Polkadot-Community-Foundation/products-devnet-issues/issues/7).

## What to do

1. **Ask the host anyway, once a session.** It costs one prompt, and a fixed app build may start
   honouring it.
2. **Classify the failure.** Don't tell the user "you denied location" when they never saw a prompt.
3. **Build a path that needs no GPS.** Something a person can do: scan a QR code, confirm a pin on a
   map, or have the other party co-sign.

```ts
import { isInsideContainer, requestDevicePermission, formatHostError } from "@parity/product-sdk-host";

// Host calls can hang rather than fail — give each one a deadline (pitfalls/host-calls-can-hang.md).
const inHost = await Promise.race([isInsideContainer(), new Promise<boolean>((r) => setTimeout(() => r(false), 1500))]);
if (inHost) {
  const r = await requestDevicePermission("Location"); // Result<boolean> from @parity/result: check r.ok
  if (!r.ok) console.warn(formatHostError(r.error));
}

async function position(): Promise<GeolocationPosition> {
  const before = (await navigator.permissions?.query({ name: "geolocation" }))?.state;
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) =>
    navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition(resolve, async (e) => {
      const after = (await navigator.permissions?.query({ name: "geolocation" }))?.state;
      // Denied without the state ever leaving "prompt": the host never answered the WebView.
      const hostGap = e.code === e.PERMISSION_DENIED && before === "prompt" && after === "prompt";
      reject(Object.assign(new Error(e.message), { kind: hostGap ? "host-callback-missing" : "user-or-os" }));
    }, { enableHighAccuracy: true, timeout: 15_000 }),
  );
}
```

### A design that settles without GPS

FARE, a delivery product, settles on **two parties who can't both lie signing the same place**. It
doesn't trust either phone's GPS:

- **Pickup:** the driver signs the venue's published pin, not their own fix.
- **Dropoff:** the customer builds the driver's commitment from the drop position and a fresh salt,
  and shows it as a QR code. The driver scans it and signs it blind. The zero-knowledge proximity
  circuit is unchanged, because it only ever needed coordinates both parties committed to.

The source is in the FARE repository (`web/src/handoff.ts`), and there is a summary in
[sources/fare.md](../sources/fare.md).

Latest detail per probe:

- `host.permissions.location` — Host granted Location. Web geolocation immediately after: still failed — User denied Geolocation
- `web.sensors.geolocation` — User denied Geolocation

  ```
  permission before : {"geolocation":"prompt"}
  permission after  : {"geolocation":"prompt"}
  
  error code            : 1
  permission before     : prompt
  permission after      : prompt
  DIAGNOSIS: permission reads 'prompt' yet the request was denied — that is the signature
  of a WebView host that never answered the permission callback, NOT a user refusal.
  'prompt' means the permission has never been decided: nothing granted, nothing denied,
  nothing stored. A genuine refusal leaves 'denied'. So the request was rejected while the
  permission remained undecided, which is what Chromium does when a request is raised and
  the embedder never resolves it — it fails closed.
  On Android the host must implement WebChromeClient.onGeolocationPermissionsShowPrompt
  and invoke its callback. The default implementation does nothing at all. Note that
  getUserMedia goes through onPermissionRequest, a DIFFERENT callback — so a runtime where
  the camera works and location does not is consistent with exactly this gap.
  ```
- `web.sensors.geolocationWatch` — Needs "web.sensors.geolocation", which came back blocked. Running anyway would test a placeholder.

## History

- 2026-07-31: failing, with the same `prompt` signature, on WebView Chromium 150 (FARE's own probe).
- 2026-09-18: unchanged on Chromium 152. The host half could not run, because the product SDK spoke
  wire codec 2 (see [pitfalls/wire-codec.md](../pitfalls/wire-codec.md)).
- 2026-09-19 09:25: the host grants `Location`, and the web API still fails.
- 2026-09-19 10:38: the most complete test so far. Android's own location dialog was allowed for
  the Polkadot app, and the Polkadot app lists Location as granted to the product. Web geolocation
  was **still refused, in 3 ms, with the state at `prompt`**. The OS and the host have both said
  yes, so what's left is the app's WebView. A refusal that fast means no prompt was ever raised:
  the app doesn't grant the WebView's geolocation request (`onGeolocationPermissionsShowPrompt`'s
  callback), or has geolocation turned off in its WebView settings.
- 2026-09-19 10:53: the same with **no permission previously granted** to the product: every prompt
  was fresh, including Android's. Refused in 5 ms, still `prompt`.

---
capability: Camera, microphone, media and peer connections
probes: [web.media.enumerateDevices, web.media.camera, web.media.microphone, web.media.imageCapture, web.media.mediaRecorder, web.media.displayMedia, web.media.pictureInPicture, web.graphics.webAudio, web.graphics.webrtc, web.graphics.webCodecs, web.media.barcodeDetector, web.limits.webrtcLoopback]

# Camera, microphone, media and peer connections

**Status (2026-09-19, codec 1, Android): the camera and microphone work through `getUserMedia`.
WebRTC between phones is not measured yet.**

- **Camera:** `getUserMedia({ video: { facingMode: "environment" } })` works, and so does a still at
  480×640. FARE captured 12.3 KiB and compressed it to 3.2 KiB in 952 ms; the canvas re-encode
  strips EXIF.
- **QR codes:** `BarcodeDetector` is built in on Android (almanac P12). Where it's missing (iOS is
  unmeasured), a JavaScript reader is about 62 KiB (`qr` 0.7.0).
- **Microphone:** it opens. `MediaRecorder` supports 6 of 8 tested formats.
- **Device labels** are empty until a grant: 3 devices showed, 0 with labels.
- **Screen capture** is absent, as expected on mobile. **Picture-in-Picture** is disabled for the
  document.

## Peer connections (calls, live data)

`RTCPeerConnection` exists and gathers ICE candidates: 4 in 158 ms on 2026-09-19. **WebCodecs**
supports all 10 tested configurations.

**A data channel opens inside the app** (two peer connections in one page, 2026-09-19 11:31). But
it took **4.4 s** to open, against 0.2 s in desktop Chrome, then 1.6 s at 14:06. It moved 1 MiB at
6.4 and then 5.6 MiB/s. Budget several seconds for a channel to open. A
non-trickle offer cut to its essentials (ufrag, password, fingerprint, 2 candidates) was **387 B**:
it fits in one 512-byte statement, with little to spare. More candidates, such as a TURN relay's,
would push it past one statement. So compress the essentials, or split them across the offer and
the answer.

**QR codes:** `BarcodeDetector` decoded a generated QR code in 174 ms, and lists 13 formats.

What is **not measured**:

- two phones connecting inside the app, after a `WebRtc` grant (almanac P13)
- two phones on different cellular networks, where carrier-grade NAT usually needs a TURN relay

The plan being built is Statement Store signalling with a minified, non-trickle SDP: one
statement per side, replaced in place. See [statement-store.md](statement-store.md) and
[sources/fare.md](../sources/fare.md).

# Network

**Status (2026-09-19, codec 1, Android): open.** `fetch` works same-origin, cross-origin (CORS)
and streaming. WebSocket to public RPC nodes works, and SSE and WebTransport are present.
`sendBeacon` is refused.

- **No content policy you can read.** The page has no CSP meta tag, and a header policy can't be
  read from script. almanac P10 found nothing blocked: the devnet IPFS gateway, People-chain and
  Bulletin RPC nodes were all reachable.
- **`navigator.sendBeacon` returns `false`**: the request is refused. Analytics and "flush on
  unload" code that relies on it silently loses data. Use `fetch(..., { keepalive: true })`, and
  test that it works.
- **The devnet IPFS gateway** (`https://devnet-ipfs.api.polkadotcommunity.foundation`) serves
  Bulletin content under both SHA-256 and BLAKE2b-256 CIDs, in about 400–600 ms. It serves
  Bulletin, not the public IPFS network.
- `navigator.connection` reports the link type (`4g`).

---
capability: Notifications and background reach

# Notifications

**Status (2026-09-19, codec 1, Android): use the host's notification manager.** The web routes are
absent: `Notification`, service workers and `PushManager` don't exist in the app.

## Use it

```ts
import { getNotificationManager, requestDevicePermission } from "@parity/product-sdk-host";
await requestDevicePermission("Notifications");
const n = await getNotificationManager();                  // null when unavailable
// scheduledAt is a bigint (almanac passes BigInt(ms since epoch)); omit it to show now.
const id = await n!.push({ text: "Your order is ready", scheduledAt: BigInt(Date.now() + 120_000) });
await n!.cancel(id);
```

- **Scheduled notifications fire with the Polkadot app closed.** A reminder scheduled two minutes
  out arrived with the app closed, on two separate builds (almanac P3). That makes reminders
  possible without a server.
- A server can't reach a closed Product through web push, because there is none. No host call for
  server-sent push has been found or measured either.

## Limits (2026-09-19)

| | |
|---|---|
| Text length | 100,000 characters accepted, the largest tried |
| Scheduled at once | 30 of 30 accepted |
| A year ahead | accepted |

Only acceptance was measured: nothing here checks how long a text the system notification actually
displays.

## Don't

- **Don't feature-detect web push by `navigator.serviceWorker`.** The property exists, but
  registration throws "ServiceWorker is not available" and `PushManager` is absent. It is a
  half-implemented API: the check passes and the call fails. Detect `PushManager` and a successful
  registration, or skip web push inside the app.

# Payments

**Status (2026-09-19, codec 1, Android): not usable yet.** The host's payment manager exists, but
its balance subscription delivered nothing in 3 s, not even a zero. The web Payment Request API
is absent.

```ts
import { getPaymentManager } from "@parity/product-sdk-host";
const pm = await getPaymentManager();
const sub = pm!.subscribeBalance((b) => render(b));   // 2026-09-19: never called back
```

A Product can't show a balance or decide whether the user can afford something. Keep payments
out of the critical path, and handle funds with contracts the user signs for through the wallet
([identity-and-accounts.md](identity-and-accounts.md)).

**Not measured:** whether a balance ever arrives after more than 3 s. Nothing here has probed a
payment that moves funds.

<<< capabilities/permissions.md >>>

---
capability: Permissions (host and web)
probes: [host.permissions.location, host.permissions.camera, host.permissions.microphone, host.permissions.notifications, host.permissions.bluetooth, host.permissions.nfc, host.permissions.clipboard, host.permissions.openurl, host.permissions.biometrics, host.permissions.remote, web.platform.permissionsApi, web.net.permissionsPolicy]
---

# Permissions

A Product deals with **two permission systems that don't talk to each other**:

1. **Host permissions.** These are truapi's `requestDevicePermission(name)` and `requestPermission(…)`.
   The Polkadot app shows its own prompt and returns a `Result<boolean>`.
2. **Web permissions.** These are the Android WebView's, for geolocation, camera, clipboard and so
   on. The host has to answer the WebView's callbacks for them.

A host grant doesn't imply the web API works. Location is the proof: the host grants it and
`navigator.geolocation` still fails ([location.md](location.md)). Camera and microphone do work
through `getUserMedia` ([media-and-calls.md](media-and-calls.md)).

## Device permissions

`requestDevicePermission` takes one of: `Location`, `Camera`, `Microphone`, `Notifications`,
`Bluetooth`, `NFC`, `Clipboard`, `OpenUrl`, `Biometrics`. All nine were granted on 2026-09-19. The
grant is what the host says; whether the matching web API then works is a separate row in the
matrix.

```ts
import { requestDevicePermission, formatHostError } from "@parity/product-sdk-host";
const r = await requestDevicePermission("Camera");
if (!r.ok) console.warn(formatHostError(r.error));    // @parity/result: read r.ok, never r.isOk()
else if (!r.value) console.warn("declined");
```

## Remote and resource permissions

- **`requestPermission({ tag, value })`** covers what a Product may ask the host to *do*. There
  are five variants, and all five were granted on 2026-09-19:
  - `Remote`, with `{ domains: [...] }`, for outbound network access
  - `WebRtc`
  - `ChainSubmit`
  - `PreimageSubmit`, for storing on Bulletin ([bulletin-storage.md](bulletin-storage.md))
  - `StatementSubmit`

  The submit variants are also asked for implicitly by the calls that need them. So a refusal here
  can surface later as a failure that looks unrelated.
- **`requestResourceAllocation([{ tag }])`** covers quota: `BulletinAllowance` and
  `StatementStoreAllowance`. It returns an outcome per item. `Allocated` is not the final word:
  Bulletin's allocation lands on a slot account that only the host can use.

## Web permissions that are blocked by the embedder

The app's WebView disables these for the document. The Permissions-Policy or a WebView setting
refuses them before any prompt:

- fullscreen
- Picture-in-Picture
- clipboard **read** (clipboard write works)
- Idle Detection
- Web NFC scan
- WebGPU (no adapter)

See [ui-and-display.md](ui-and-display.md) and [sensors-and-hardware.md](sensors-and-hardware.md).

<<< capabilities/statement-store.md >>>

---
capability: Statement Store (small signed messages between phones)
probes: [host.statement.subscribe, host.statement.createProof, host.statement.submit, host.limits.statementSize, host.limits.statementLatency, host.limits.statementExpiry, host.limits.statementCapacity]
---

# Statement Store

**Status (2026-09-19, codec 1, Android): works, including delivery between two phones.** sonde
submitted a statement from inside the app in 8.1 s (2026-09-19, 10:53). It is
tiny: 512 bytes per statement and about 1 KiB per account. Use it to find each other or to hold a
pointer, not to carry data.

## What it is good for

- **A rendezvous point.** Two phones derive a topic from a secret they share, such as a code shown
  as a QR. One publishes and the other subscribes. almanac P9b/P9c, 2026-09-17: phone B found phone
  A's statement, carrying A's signer, on a phone that never held A's keys.
- **A slot you overwrite.** Publishing again on the same `channel` replaces the earlier statement,
  and a fresh subscription sees only the new one. That makes it a mutable pointer, or a revocable
  share.
- **Late joiners.** A subscription also delivers statements that already exist, so whoever opens
  second still finds the offer.

## Use it

```ts
import { createProofAuthorized, formatHostError, fromHex, getStatementStore, requestResourceAllocation, toHex } from "@parity/product-sdk-host";

const store = await getStatementStore();                         // null when unavailable
// Needed before the first submit (almanac P9). Asking again does no harm.
await requestResourceAllocation([{ tag: "StatementStoreAllowance" }]);

// Expiry is (unix seconds << 32) | sequence; a later expiry makes a statement newer.
const expiry = BigInt(Math.floor((Date.now() + 3_600_000) / 1000)) << 32n;
const statement = { topics: [toHex(topic)], channel: toHex(channel), expiry, data: toHex(sealed) };
const proof = await createProofAuthorized(statement);             // the host signs
if (!proof.ok) throw new Error(formatHostError(proof.error));
await store!.submit({ ...statement, proof: proof.value });

const sub = store!.subscribe({ matchAny: [toHex(topic)] }, (page) => {
  for (const s of page.statements) if (s.data) heard(fromHex(s.data));
});
sub.onInterrupt(() => { /* the host dropped it: subscribe again after a pause */ });
```

almanac's working version is `app/src/platform/polkadot.ts` (`statementPort`).

## Limits

| Limit | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Bytes per statement | 512 | `product-sdk-statement-store` 0.6.9 constants |
| Bytes per account | ~1 KiB | same |
| Statements per account | 2 to 4 seen, **not settled** | almanac P9: three runs disagreed, and each allowance grant may add room |
| Longest expiry | 90 days accepted | almanac P9 |
| When full | `AccountFull(submittedExpiry, minExpiry)` refuses a statement that expires sooner than the shortest one held | almanac P9 |
| No expiry | **kept as the maximum (i64::MAX), and never leaves** | sonde, 2026-09-19. The SDK's 30 s default TTL does not apply to a statement submitted through the host without one |
| Latency between phones | **not measured** | — |

## Don't

- **Don't submit without an `expiry`.** The host keeps such a statement with the maximum expiry.
  Each one fills a slot that never frees. Once the account is full of them, **every statement
  with a finite expiry is refused**, because a full account refuses anything that would expire
  sooner than the shortest it holds:
  `AccountFull(submittedExpiry=…, minExpiry=9223372036854775807)`. sonde did exactly this, one
  statement per run on a fresh topic, until its account refused everything else (2026-09-19).
  Always set an expiry, and reuse a `channel` so a new statement replaces the old one.
- **It gets worse: the account can lock up completely.** On 2026-09-19 12:55, with the account
  full of no-expiry statements, even another no-expiry statement was refused:
  `AccountFull(submittedExpiry=MAX, minExpiry=MAX)`. An equal expiry is refused too, and statements
  without a channel can't be replaced. So nothing more can be published from that account, unless
  the store drops them on its own; that isn't observed yet. sonde's `sondeprobes.dot` is in this
  state.
- **Don't put plaintext in it.** Statements are public gossip, and anyone can compute a topic
  derived from a public id. Seal the data, and derive topics from a shared secret.
- **Don't assume the signer is the user.** Statements are signed by the product's allowance account,
  not by product account #0 (almanac P8). It is per product, not per user, so a user's statements
  can still be linked to each other within one product.
- **Don't stream through it.** For anything larger, open WebRTC and use statements only for the
  offer and answer. A minified, non-trickle SDP is about 150–250 bytes, which fits in one statement
  ([sources/fare.md](../sources/fare.md)). WebRTC between two phones inside the app is **not
  measured yet** (almanac P13).

<<< pitfalls/deploy-with-a-key.md >>>

# Publish with a local deploy key, not the phone

**Symptom:** `pad deploy` gets as far as "Link content" and reverts with
`Revive.ContractReverted`. Or `pad` refuses because the name "is already owned by 0x…", and that
address is one you don't recognise. `pad whoami` shows "Product address: unresolved".

**Cause:** when `pad` signs through the phone, the signer is a **product account the wallet
derives and never reveals.** The app answers signing requests but never answers `pad`'s request
for that account's key, so `pad` *displays* the root account instead. Then:

- A name registered in August is owned by the account the wallet signed as then. That account came
  from the old public derivation (`product-sdk-keys` 0.3).
- A name registered in September was handed to the root `pad` displayed.
- The September app signs as a **third** account. It derives from a key the wallet holds
  (`product-sdk-keys` 0.4), so it **can't be computed** off the phone. It was found by reading the
  signer out of the raw extrinsic on chain.

So neither name can be updated from the phone.

## Do

Hold a deploy key on your computer and run `pad` as a library:

- The key owns the name and signs DotNS.
- One of `pad`'s pool accounts signs the Bulletin upload. An owner key isn't authorized to store on
  devnet, and a pool account can spend upload quota but never own or repoint the name.
- Pass **`transferToSignedInUser: false`**. `pad` turns it on whenever a login session exists, and
  would hand the finished name to the phone account.

```js
import { derivePoolAccounts } from "@polkadot-community-foundation/polkadot-app-deploy";
import { deploy } from "@polkadot-community-foundation/polkadot-app-deploy/deploy";
const pool = derivePoolAccounts();
const up = pool[Math.floor(Math.random() * pool.length)];
await deploy("dist", "yourlabel.dot", {
  mnemonic,                          // the deploy key, from a mode-600 file outside the repo
  storageSigner: up.signer,
  storageSignerAddress: up.address,
  transferToSignedInUser: false,
  env: "devnet",
  jsMerkle: true,
});
```

Working scripts: sonde's `tools/deploy-key.mjs` and `tools/deploy.mjs`, and almanac's equivalents.
Before registering, check the name's owner with a read-only lookup (`tools/whois.mjs`). Refuse if
the owner is not your key, and make registering an explicit, typed-back step.

## Also

- **`PRODUCT_ID` must equal the `.dot` label.** The host keys product accounts, local storage and
  allowances by it. If they drift apart, host probes exercise an identity that never published
  anything.
- **Labels:** a signer with no personhood can register a base of **9 or more letters**, with or
  without two trailing digits. A base of 6–8 letters with two digits needs Personhood Lite. `pad`'s
  preflight is not a stopping point: for an eligible name it goes straight on to registration. So
  never loop `pad` over candidate names; each one it's allowed to register, it registers, at about
  10 PAS.
- **Debugging a revert:** read the signer off the raw extrinsic before forming a theory. An
  afternoon went to two wrong ones.

<<< pitfalls/dotns-registrar-moved.md >>>

# The devnet DotNS registrar moved

**Symptom:** a read-only ownership lookup says a name you just registered has no owner, or `pad`
and your own scripts disagree about a name.

**Cause:** on the Paseo Asset Hub EVM (`https://eth-rpc-testnet.polkadot.io/`, chain id 420420417),
the DotNS registrar was redeployed. Names registered after the move exist only in the new one.

| Contract | Address (as `pad` 0.16.6 has it, 2026-09-18) |
|---|---|
| Registrar (ERC-721; tokenId = namehash of `label.dot`) | `0xc609e0c2DAB4433d55a32FB098Db8788C1956302` |
| Personhood rules (`POP_RULES`) | `0xD5Ee34610F06f7FF4668aB4fabE2393B65a43AE7` |
| Registry | `0xb052E5EfC5ADEff1f21d48DEfb5169Cb394A1a73` |
| Content resolver | `0x7e75491ecfb04900EB05ee63CABA2B33900aABB5` |

**Do:** read contract addresses from the installed `pad` package rather than hard-coding them, or
re-check them whenever `pad` updates. sonde's and almanac's `tools/whois.mjs` show a read-only
lookup.

<<< pitfalls/host-calls-can-hang.md >>>

# Host calls can hang instead of failing

Many host calls, when they can't do what was asked, **never settle**: no value, no error. A Product
that awaits one without a deadline freezes, and never reaches its fallback.

| Call | When it goes silent | Seen |
|---|---|---|
| Every host call | the SDK speaks a wire codec the app doesn't ([wire-codec.md](wire-codec.md)) | sonde 2026-09-18 |
| `isInsideContainer()` | outside the app: nobody is there to answer | by design |
| `preimageManager.lookup(key, cb)` | the content is absent, or was stored under SHA-256: there is no "not found" | almanac P7, sonde |
| `cloudStorage.fetch(cid)` | the same, until the SDK's own 30 s timeout | almanac P7, sonde |
| `getChainSpec(genesis)` | any chain other than Paseo Asset Hub, including the devnet chains the host itself stores on | sonde 2026-09-19 |
| `paymentManager.subscribeBalance(cb)` | always, so far | sonde 2026-09-19 |
| `cloudStorage.upload` | S1: hung 180 s with no error | FARE |
| `wallet.signMessage` | until the user answers the prompt | by design |

## Do

```ts
export function withTimeout<T>(p: Promise<T>, ms: number, what: string): Promise<T> {
  let t: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>;
  return Promise.race([
    p,
    new Promise<never>((_, reject) => { t = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error(`${what}: no answer in ${ms / 1000} s`)), ms); }),
  ]).finally(() => clearTimeout(t));
}
```

Suggested deadlines, from measurements:

| Kind of call | Deadline |
|---|---|
| Detection | 1.5 s |
| A prompt the user must read and tap | 60 s |
| A Bulletin upload | 120–180 s (1 MiB took 41 s) |
| A lookup the host holds | 30 s (a hit comes back in under 1 s) |

For subscriptions, resolve on the first useful callback, unsubscribe when the timer fires, and
treat silence as "unknown", never as "absent".

<<< pitfalls/sdk-gotchas.md >>>

# SDK gotchas

Small things in `@parity/product-sdk*` that cost an afternoon each.

- **Two `Result` conventions.** The top-level wrappers in `@parity/product-sdk-host`
  (`requestDevicePermission`, `requestPermission`, `deriveEntropy`, `getChainSpec`, `navigateTo`,
  `requestResourceAllocation`, `createProofAuthorized`…) return `@parity/result`'s
  `{ ok, value } | { ok, error }`. The raw truapi client and `AccountsProvider` return neverthrow's
  `ResultAsync`, which has `.match()` and **no `.ok`**. Reading `.ok` off the second yields
  `undefined`, so every call looks like a failure.
- **`BulletinAllowance`, not `BulletInAllowance`.** The TypeScript type spells it with a capital I,
  and that spelling throws. Cast: `{ tag: "BulletinAllowance", value: undefined } as never`.
- **`Allocated` doesn't mean an upload will work.** Through `cloudStorage.upload` it never does
  (`Invalid: Payment`). Use `getPreimageManager().submit()`
  ([capabilities/bulletin-storage.md](../capabilities/bulletin-storage.md)).
- **`createApp`'s cloud storage defaults to `"paseo"`.** Pass `cloudStorage: { environment: "devnet" }`
  when you publish to devnet, or `createApp` throws that the chain isn't supported.
- **Connected isn't selected.** After `wallet.connect()`, call `wallet.selectAccount(address)`, or
  storage calls stall.
- **Statement expiry is `(unix seconds << 32) | sequence`**, as a bigint. **Leaving it out does
  not mean "short-lived".** The host keeps the statement with the maximum expiry, forever, and a
  handful of those will block every later statement that has a real expiry
  (`AccountFull(…, minExpiry=9223372036854775807)`). See
  [statement-store](../capabilities/statement-store.md).
- **The host's lookup takes a bare 32-byte digest**, not a CID. `cidToPreimageKey` accepts SHA-256
  CIDs, but only BLAKE2b-256 content is found.
- **`getAnonymousAlias()` returns `null`.** Don't design on the Ring VRF alias yet.

<<< pitfalls/wire-codec.md >>>

# The TrUAPI wire codec must match the app

**Symptom:** inside the app, **every** host call hangs, or fails at the handshake with "the host did
not answer on wire codec 2". Container detection still says you're inside the app, and nothing else
works.

**Cause:** `@parity/truapi` changed its wire codec from 1 to 2 in 0.16.0. A Product built on codec 2
talks past an app that only answers codec 1. The app doesn't reject the message; it just never
answers.

**As of 2026-09-19 the Polkadot app on Android answers codec 1 only.** The last SDK set on codec 1:

```json
{
  "@parity/product-sdk": "0.27.0",
  "@parity/product-sdk-host": "0.19.1",
  "@parity/product-sdk-keys": "0.3.24",
  "@parity/product-sdk-statement-store": "0.6.9",
  "@parity/product-sdk-terminal": "0.8.2",
  "@parity/truapi": "0.13.1"
}
```

`product-sdk-host` 0.20 and later depend on truapi ≥ 0.16, which is codec 2.

## Do

- **Pin exact versions** (no `^`). A routine `npm update` moves you onto codec 2.
- **Check what you shipped:** `import { TRUAPI_CODEC_VERSION } from "@parity/truapi"`, and show it
  in a debug footer.
- **Give the handshake and the first host call a deadline**, so a mismatch reads as "host didn't
  answer" and not as a spinner that never stops.
- **When a new app ships,** run a probe built on the newer SDK (sonde records the codec in every
  run). The first run where a codec 2 handshake passes is when to move.

Measured by sonde on 2026-09-18: a codec 2 build failed every handshake. Pinned back to codec 1 on
2026-09-19, the handshake passed in 36 ms.

<<< sources/almanac-probe.md >>>

# almanac's device probe (P1–P14)

[almanac](https://github.com/Baronvonbonbon/almanac) is a private cycle tracker built as a Product.
Before building on the platform, it measured it: a probe app published as `almanacprobe.dot`, and
checks named P1–P14. The full answers are in
[docs/PROBE-REPORT.md](https://github.com/Baronvonbonbon/almanac/blob/main/docs/PROBE-REPORT.md).
Device: Pixel 10 Pro XL, Android 16, Polkadot app 1.0.0 (40), 2026-09-13 to 17, on
`product-sdk` 0.27.0 and `product-sdk-host` 0.19.1 (codec 1).

| Check | Answer | Used on |
|---|---|---|
| P1 host storage | survives restarts and new builds; 4 MiB in one record, 1.2–1.3 s. App update and reinstall not tested | [local-storage](../capabilities/local-storage.md) |
| P2 `deriveEntropy` | same bytes across restarts and builds. Reinstall and a second phone not tested | [identity-and-accounts](../capabilities/identity-and-accounts.md) |
| P3 scheduled notification | fires with the app closed | [notifications](../capabilities/notifications.md) |
| P4 exports | nothing leaves as a file; clipboard write and picked-file read work | [files-and-sharing](../capabilities/files-and-sharing.md) |
| P5 phone backups | not run | — |
| P6 `cloudStorage.upload` | always `Invalid: Payment`; the product account holds no authorization | [bulletin-storage](../capabilities/bulletin-storage.md) |
| P6b preimage submit | works; paid from a hidden slot account's quota (10 transactions and 4 MiB a claim, ~14 days) | [bulletin-storage](../capabilities/bulletin-storage.md) |
| P6c upload sizes | 16 KiB 6.7 s, 64 KiB 10.0 s, 256 KiB 16.8 s, 1 MiB 41.4 s; charged exactly by size | [bulletin-storage](../capabilities/bulletin-storage.md) |
| P7 reads and retention | the host finds BLAKE2b-256 only; the gateway finds both; retention being measured (~2 weeks) | [bulletin-storage](../capabilities/bulletin-storage.md) |
| P8 which account signs | uploads: product account #0; statements: another account, not #0–#2 | [identity-and-accounts](../capabilities/identity-and-accounts.md) |
| P9 Statement Store | replace-in-place works; subscriptions deliver existing statements; 90-day expiry accepted; capacity per account not settled | [statement-store](../capabilities/statement-store.md) |
| P9b/P9c between phones | delivery works, found by topic | [statement-store](../capabilities/statement-store.md) |
| P10 network | gateway and RPC nodes reachable; nothing blocked | [network](../capabilities/network.md) |
| P11 crypto speed | scrypt N=2¹⁶ 169 ms; XChaCha 1 MiB 24 ms; BLAKE2b 1 MiB 18 ms | [compute-and-crypto](../capabilities/compute-and-crypto.md) |
| P12 theme and camera | the host theme, not the phone's; camera and `BarcodeDetector` work | [app-and-system](../capabilities/app-and-system.md), [media-and-calls](../capabilities/media-and-calls.md) |
| P13 WebRTC between phones | not run | [media-and-calls](../capabilities/media-and-calls.md) |
| P14 QR codes on iOS | not run | — |

None of this is in `runs/` yet. almanac's report predates the run schema and uses its own check ids.

<<< sources/fare.md >>>

# FARE: designs that work around the gaps

[FARE](https://github.com/Baronvonbonbon/fare) is a delivery and ride Product. Its contracts are on
Paseo Asset Hub, and its driver and customer surfaces run inside the Polkadot app. Three of its
designs answer gaps measured here. The detail is in FARE's `docs/POLKADOT-PLATFORM-PLAN.md`
(§4.7, §4.10–§4.12).

## Settling without GPS (built)

Location is unavailable ([capabilities/location.md](../capabilities/location.md)). FARE's guarantee
was never the geometry; it is **two parties with opposite interests signing the same thing**:

- **Pickup:** the driver signs the venue's published pin.
- **Dropoff:** the customer builds the driver's commitment from the drop position and a fresh salt,
  and shows it as a QR code (`makeDropoffRequest`). The driver scans it and signs it blind
  (`signDropoffRequest`).

The Groth16 proximity circuit is unchanged, and a test runs it against a real proof
(`test/gps-free-settlement.test.ts`). Code: `web/src/handoff.ts`, `web/src/geo.ts`,
`web/src/host.ts`.

## Signalling over the Statement Store, data over WebRTC (designed)

A statement holds 512 bytes, and an account about 1 KiB. So the Statement Store carries only the
connection setup, and WebRTC carries the payload:

- **Non-trickle, minified SDP.** Wait for ICE gathering to finish, then send only ufrag, password,
  DTLS fingerprint and a few candidates. The estimate was 150–250 bytes; measured inside the app
  (2026-09-19), it was **387 bytes with 2 candidates**. That still fits one 512-byte statement, but
  only just. Rebuild the full SDP from a template
  at the other end.
- **One statement per side per order, replaced in place:** the offer, then the answer.
- **Sealed, on a topic derived from a secret the parties share.** Candidates carry IP addresses, and
  statements are public.

Risks, in order: carrier-grade NAT on cellular (plan a TURN relay), linkage through the product's
allowance account, and both parties having to be online.

## Bulletin as dispute evidence (designed)

Delivery photos go to Bulletin through the host, and live about 14 days. That lifetime is the
evidence window, if:

1. The photo's BLAKE2b-256 key is **committed in something signed at the event**, not cited later.
2. The dispute clock fits inside the storage clock: for example, open within 72 h and rule within
   10 days. Re-uploading the same bytes renews them under the same key.
3. Only the arbiter can read it: sealed, with the key encrypted to the arbiter at filing.
4. The arbiter can fetch outside the app, through the devnet IPFS gateway.

Limit: Bulletin is on the devnet, which resets, while the contracts are on Paseo. Fine for a demo,
not for production.

<<< sources/sonde.md >>>

# sonde: measuring from inside the app

[sonde](https://github.com/Baronvonbonbon/sonde) is a Product that probes the platform from inside
the Polkadot app. It is published at `sondeprobes.dot`. It runs about 130 probes over the host API
and the web platform. Every probe is bounded by a deadline, so a hang reads as `timeout` instead of
a frozen page. It separates **absent** (`unsupported`), **forbidden** (`blocked`) and **broken**
(`fail`), and records a diagnosis such as `host-callback-missing` or `policy-blocked-by-embedder`.

## Tiers

- **T0 detect** and **T1 invoke** have no side effects.
- **T2 prompt** shows host prompts; tap through them.
- **T3 spend** writes to chain: a Bulletin upload and a statement. It runs only on chains in sonde's
  spend allowlist, which holds the devnet "Next" chains and refuses mainnet by name.

## Adding a run to this repository

1. Open `sondeprobes.dot` in the Polkadot app, run the tiers you're comfortable with, and tap
   **Copy record**. The record has addresses, keys and picked file names removed. It leaves out
   language, time zone and screen size.
2. Save it as `runs/<key>.json`. The key is in the record: date, wire codec, `product-sdk-host`
   version, OS and the time of capture.
3. If you skipped a probe by hand, or read the app version off the phone, add a line to `notes` or
   set `runtime.appVersion`.
4. Run `node tools/build.mjs` and open a pull request.

Reports copied before the Copy record button existed can be converted with
`tools/import-sonde-markdown.mjs` (see `raw/`).

## When a result is the probe's fault

A result that measured a bug in the probe is kept, with a `retracted` note saying what was wrong.
The matrix strikes it out. Three from 2026-09-19 were retracted:

- a made-up genesis hash, so `getChainSpec` waited forever
- a SHA-256 CID that the host's lookup can never find
- `navigateTo` pointed at the page's own URL, which reloads it

All three are fixed in sonde. The 10:05 run confirmed the fixes: the genesis resolved, the read
passed in 245 ms, and `navigateTo` returned without a reload. That run showed a fourth problem of
the same kind: sonde's spend allowlist didn't hold the one chain the host resolved (Paseo Asset
Hub), so the upload and statement-submit probes were refused again. Those are retracted too, and the
allowlist is fixed. Read a probe's source before filing a platform bug on its result.
